• Added support for the SM9 identity-based key encapsulation mechanism (GM/T 0044.4-2016), built on an R-ate pairing over a 256-bit Barreto-Naehrig curve. The lightweight implementation follows the standard BouncyCastle package layout: SM9KEMGenerator / SM9KEMExtractor in org.bouncycastle.crypto.kems, the encryption master key-pair generator (which derives a user's decapsulation key from the user's identity) in org.bouncycastle.crypto.generators, the key parameter classes in org.bouncycastle.crypto.params, with the underlying BN curve, extension-field tower and R-ate pairing arithmetic in org.bouncycastle.math.ec.sm9. The BouncyCastle provider exposes it through the GM family as KeyGenerator.SM9-KEM (via KEMGenerateSpec / KEMExtractSpec), with the KGC's master key pair from KeyPairGenerator.SM9-ENC (round-tripping through KeyFactory.SM9); a user's key pair is generated from the master private key via the org.bouncycastle.jcajce.interfaces.SM9EncMasterPrivateKey interface's generateUserKeyPair(id) - the deterministic KGC derivation identity-based schemes call key extraction - and a sender forms a recipient's public key from the published master public key alone via SM9EncMasterPublicKey.getUserPublicKey(id). The requested key length drives SM9's own GM/T 0044.4 KDF directly. Verified against the official GM/T 0044.5-2016 worked example.

• The SM9-KEM is now also available through the JDK 21 javax.crypto.KEM API as KEM.SM9-KEM: the encapsulator takes a recipient public key from SM9EncMasterPublicKey.getUserPublicKey(id), the decapsulator the matching user private key. By default (a null spec, or KTSParameterSpec.Builder.withNoKdf()) the shared secret is the mechanism's own GM/T 0044.4 KDF output at the requested size - the interoperable form; a KTSParameterSpec KDF may optionally be layered on top for generic use, in which case the GM/T 0044.4 KDF first produces a 256-bit shared secret for the configured KDF (note this form does not interoperate with other SM9 implementations). The SM9 private keys (the encryption master private key and users' decapsulation keys) now also honour the JCA javax.security.auth.Destroyable contract: destroy() invalidates the underlying key material - dropping the immutable secret values and zeroizing the carried identity - after which isDestroyed() reflects the state and the secret-bearing operations (getEncoded(), generateUserKeyPair(), decapsulation) throw IllegalStateException; the published master public key, and so the sender side of the scheme, is unaffected.

• Added SM9 identity-based public-key encryption (GM/T 0044.4-2016), exposed through the BouncyCastle provider as Cipher.SM9. The lightweight implementation is SM9Engine in org.bouncycastle.crypto.engines, reusing the encryption master/user key infrastructure of the SM9 KEM; a sender encrypts to the recipient's public key, formed from the published master public key and the recipient's identity via SM9EncMasterPublicKey.getUserPublicKey(id) - the same recipient key the SM9-KEM encapsulates to - and the recipient decrypts with the private key derived for its identity via SM9EncMasterPrivateKey.generateUserKeyPair(id). GM/T 0044.4 defines two data-encapsulation modes: the default wraps the message with the SM4 block cipher (Cipher.SM9), while SM9/XOR/NoPadding uses the KDF as a stream cipher; the ciphertext is emitted as the GM/T 0080-2020 SM9Cipher structure (enType, C1, C3, C2) and is self-describing, so a single Cipher.SM9 decrypts either mode. Verified against the official GM/T 0044.5-2016 Annex D worked example.

  • Added the SM9 identity-based digital signature algorithm (GM/T 0044.2-2016), exposed through the BouncyCastle provider as Signature.SM9. The lightweight implementation is SM9Signer in org.bouncycastle.crypto.signers, with the signature master key-pair generator in org.bouncycastle.crypto.generators and the key parameter classes in org.bouncycastle.crypto.params. The master key pair comes from KeyPairGenerator.SM9-SIGN and round-trips through KeyFactory.SM9; a user's key pair is derived from the master private key via the SM9SignMasterPrivateKey.generateUserKeyPair(id) interface method (the deterministic KGC extraction, hid = 0x01), and a verifier forms the signer's public key from the published master public key and the signer's identity alone via SM9SignMasterPublicKey.getUserPublicKey(id) - no AlgorithmParameterSpec is involved, matching the SM9 encryption side. The signature private keys honour the Destroyable contract in the same way as the SM9 encryption keys, and the JCA signature is the GM/T 0080-2020 SM9Signature structure (DER: h, S). Verified against the official GM/T 0044.5-2016 Annex A worked example, including zero-length messages.
